title: Compliance attestation workflow for external model onboarding
creator: Aisha Varma
description: Create a single, auditable onboarding workflow for third-party and externally contributed models that enforces legal attestations, flags restricted weights, and publishes a verified performance profile. This ticket covers UX and API requirements for the attestation step, acceptance criteria for automated license parsing, the enforcement points that block deployment into hosted/dedicated/private slots, and the telemetry surfaced in Console to support audits. It does NOT include implementation of kernel optimizations or quantization — those are separate engineering tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A guided attestation form exists in the onboarding flow that captures license type, provenance notes, and one-click attestation by an authorized user.
Automated license scanner returns a structured result; ambiguous licenses produce a "needs-review" flag and block publish until resolved.
Restricted-weights ruleset (internal list + heuristic model fingerprinting) flags models and attaches a mandatory mitigation plan before enabling serving.
Model version pinning UI shows the approved version and prevents promoting un-attested versions to production routes.
Performance profile (latency, cost, memory footprints) is published to the model catalog after a verified benchmark run; profiles include an origin tag and checksum of artifacts.
All attestation actions and reviewer approvals are stored in an audit log accessible in Console and exportable for compliance review.
APIs return clear error codes for blocked onboarding attempts (e.g., 409_LICENSE_ISSUE, 403_RESTRICTED_WEIGHTS).
decisions: Prefer a hybrid approach: automated license parsing + human-in-the-loop review for ambiguous cases to balance throughput and legal accuracy.
Implement initial restricted-weights enforcement as a soft-block in sandbox environments and a hard-block for hosted public endpoints until policy signoff.
Store attestations in the control plane (encrypted) rather than in the model artifact to simplify rollbacks and revocations.
Expose a machine-readable attestation object (JSON) so infra and Dedicated deployments can enforce policies consistently.
Defer full KMS/HSM integration for attestation signing to a follow-up ticket; use RBAC-scoped signing keys for MVP.

2026-03-01: Legal provided initial restricted-weights criteria. Need to formalize exception process for research partnerships.
2026-03-05: Design review — iterative wireframes attached. PM asked to reduce friction for small OSS model uploads by allowing prefilled attestations via GitHub meta-data import.
2026-03-08: Security flagged need for tamper-evident audit logs; suggested HMAC signing of attestation records (deferred to security ticket).
2026-03-10: Product review: accept draft acceptance criteria; requested addition of API error codes and Console remediation workflow (see links).
implementation_notes: MVP scope: attestation form + license scanner integration (OSS scanner) + soft-block enforcement + Console UI for reviewer approvals.
Follow-ups: HSM-signed attestations, automated remediation suggestions, integration with Dedicated deployment admission controller.
Engineering should create separate ENG tickets for: license-scanner service, attestation storage schema, Console reviewer UI, API error spec, and audit export endpoint.
Design artifacts: low-fi + hi-fi flows available in Drive link; incorporate an accessibility pass before launch.
review_feedback: Legal (2026-03-02): Add requirement to capture a source-of-truth URL and checksum for any uploaded weights/artifacts.
Security (2026-03-08): Recommend moving from soft-block to hard-block for any models with cryptomining or weaponization-related license clauses — placeholder until policy final.
Design (2026-03-05): Simplify attestation copy and include inline help for common license types.
Platform (2026-03-09): Suggest exposing an API hook so CI can auto-advance attestation when the uploader’s GitHub organization has a verified business account.
PM (2026-03-10): Add user stories for enterprise flows (delegated reviewers, SSO-scoped approvals).
